title: Which Investors Will Get Rich From Anthropic’s IPO?
description: When Anthropic goes public in a blockbuster offering, which investors will profit? The answer says a lot about how much start-up investing has changed over the years.
author: Erin Griffith

title: Noise and Motion Monitors in Their Homes? These Tenants Say No.
description: The public housing authority in Concord, N.H., installed monitoring devices in 300 homes. Tenants are now suing to remove the Minut sensors.
author: Kashmir Hill

title: In a Big Win, Google Won’t Have to Break Up Its Ad Tech Business, Court Rules
description: In a long-awaited decision, a federal judge said Google must change its ad tech business to address antitrust issues, but did not disclose the measures.
author: David McCabe and Tripp Mickle

title: Justice Dept. Sides With OpenAI in New York Times Copyright Suit
description: The department argued in a court filing that OpenAI legally used articles by The New York Times to develop A.I., adding that national security depended on American tech dominance.
author: Karen Weise and Mike Isaac

title: Uber Lays Off 10% of Employees in Sweeping Reorganization
description: The layoffs affect about 3,300 workers, as Chief Executive Dara Khosrowshahi bets on a “leaner organization.”
author: Emmy Martin

title: Patrick Gleeson, Who Made Synthesizers Part of Jazz, Dies at 91
description: He abandoned a job teaching college English in the 1960s to become a pioneer of the instrument, playing onstage with Herbie Hancock’s jazz band.
author: Alex Williams

title: Get to Know Your Phone’s Built-In Emergency Kit
description: In times of natural disasters and other dangers, special features tucked away on your iPhone or Android device could help make a difference.
author: J. D. Biersdorfer

title: Social Media and the Myth of the Big Tobacco Moment
description: Smoking used to be everywhere, the way Facebook, TikTok, Snap, YouTube and Instagram are now. Society decided to break the habit, but it took a long time.
author: David Streitfeld

title: Missouri Voters Appear to Recall City Councilman Over Data Center Support
description: Initial results showed that residents of Independence, Mo., voted overwhelmingly to recall an official who backed billions of dollars in tax breaks for a data center.
author: David McCabe and Lauren McCarthy

title: Map Apps Are Handling Trump’s Renaming of Lake Ontario to Lake America Differently
description: Navigation companies face a new dilemma after President Trump ordered Lake Ontario to be renamed Lake America.
author: Victor Mather

title: John Ternus Replaces Tim Cook as Apple CEO
description: Big technology and management changes are greeting John Ternus, whose long-serving predecessor, Tim Cook, will stay on as executive chair.
author: Kalley Huang

title: FTC and 22 States Sue Amazon Over Advertising Practices
description: Regulators say the e-commerce giant forced more than a million advertisers to pay more than they should have. The company denies the claims.
author: Karen Weise

title: Influencers Have a Lot to Say About Politics. Many Are Quietly Paid for It.
description: Their videos have proliferated on social media, but the payments are frequently hidden from viewers.
author: Ken Bensinger and Stuart A. Thompson

title: How Meta’s $17.1 Billion Social Media Settlement Came Together
description: State attorneys general spent months in negotiations. Then, as its legal losses mounted, the social media giant’s new top lawyer brought a huge settlement to the table.
author: Cecilia Kang and Eli Tan

title: Prediction Markets Should Be Regulated as Gambling, Appeals Court Says
description: The outcome contradicted an earlier appeals court decision. Federal regulators said the split rulings called for resolution by the Supreme Court.
author: Lauren McCarthy

title: What Meta’s $17 Billion Settlement Means
description: Our reporter Cecilia Kang explains Meta’s settlement of a lawsuit claiming that the company’s social media platforms had harmed teenage users.
author: Cecilia Kang, Nikolay Nikolov, Paul Abowd, Alexandra Ostasiewicz and June Kim

title: Why Countries Are Pushing Social Media Bans Despite Their Flaws
description: Proposals for curbing social media use among children have wide support, but critics say they are ineffective.
author: John Yoon

title: Meta Shifts the Blame + Do Data Center Bans Work? + The Final HatGPT
description: Meta negotiated an unusual provision in their landmark settlement: If TikTok and YouTube also agree to penalties and changes to their products, Meta will pay more.
author: Kevin Roose, Casey Newton, Rachel Cohn, Whitney Jones, Vjeran Pavic, Alyssa Moxley, Dan Powell, Elisheba Ittoop, Marion Lozano and Rowan Niemisto

title: Trump Administration’s Blacklisting of Anthropic Was Illegal, Judge Rules
description: The government retaliated against the A.I. start-up “for constitutionally protected expressive activities,” a federal judge in California wrote.
author: Sheera Frenkel

title: OpenAI and 100 Others Warn That Window to Defend Against A.I. Attacks Is Narrowing
description: In an open letter, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and others said that a wave of A.I.-enabled cyberattacks was coming and that organizations and governments needed to prepare themselves.
author: Kate Conger
